chunks: As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who used to toil on the sea. I damaged it because there was a king after them who used to seize every ship by force.
ai.seo_question: Why did Khidr damage the boat of the poor fishermen?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind Khidr's seemingly destructive act, noting that the vessel belonged to poor fishermen and was damaged to preempt its confiscation by a tyrannical king who seized ships by force. This interpretation highlights the concept of *khafi* (hidden wisdom) in Shia exegesis, where a temporary loss preserves a greater benefit for the owners. The narrative underscores the balance between apparent loss and actual preservation in divine decree.
